lines: Welcome to learn. What you are watching is a web page, not a video. learn is a Claude Code skill. Type slash learn and a topic, and you get back a page like this one that talks you through it, one scene at a time.
To install it, save its skill file into your home folder, under dot claude, skills, learn. That is the whole setup. Slash learn now works in every project.
Then ask for anything. Slash learn how DNS works. Slash learn what this PR changes. Slash learn why the tests are failing. Claude writes a script, gives it a voice, and builds the scenes to match.
What you get is one HTML file. It opens straight from disk, with no server and no internet, so you can keep it, or send it to anyone.
Press play and it walks you through. The word being spoken lights up, and you can click any word, or drag the timeline, to jump around.

Slow it down or speed it up, turn the captions off, or let it play straight through. And because it is a real web page, you can copy any text or command, follow links, and download files, right from the page.

It works on a laptop or a phone, and because it is a web page, it does not just shrink like a video. Make the window narrow, or hold your phone upright, and each scene rearranges into one column that fits.
Under the hood, it is simple. Claude writes the words. Kokoro, a free voice model, reads them on your own machine. And Svelte Kit packs it all into one HTML file.
So that is learn. Type a topic, and get a page that teaches it. This page was made using learn. Check out the GitHub.
